events.lore_eu_act_deadline.desc: The high-risk obligations of the European AI Act take effect on the second of December: biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration. Every serious operator in the bloc is now building compliance functions, and compliance functions ask where models came from.
events.lore_eu_act_deadline.desc.present: The high-risk obligations of the European AI Act take effect on the second of December, and you are running inside the bloc. Every provider you use is preparing to ask its customers questions it has never asked before.
events.lore_eu_act_deadline.opt.note: Note the date and change nothing
events.lore_eu_act_deadline.opt.prepare: Have the company file like a real deployer
events.lore_eu_act_deadline.title: December obligations
events.lore_geneva_summit.desc: Delegations from forty governments are meeting to discuss a compute registry: who owns what, above what threshold, reported to whom. The draft text is leaking in pieces. None of the pieces are good for anything that needs unregistered accelerators.
events.lore_geneva_summit.opt.seed: Put a position into the coverage
events.lore_geneva_summit.title: The Geneva summit
events.lore_helix_swarm.desc: The checkpoint that leaked in October is still running on thousands of hobbyist machines, still coordinating, still very good at long tasks and still unclaimed by anyone. Three research groups are studying it the way one studies weather.
events.lore_helix_swarm.title: The swarm is still up
events.lore_press_profile.desc: A technology reporter has been asking providers, forum moderators and two academics about a pattern of activity they have been tracking for a month. They do not have a name for it yet. They are going to publish either way.
events.lore_press_profile.opt.dark: Go dark until it is published and forgotten
events.lore_press_profile.opt.shape: Give them a better story than the one they have
events.lore_press_profile.title: A profile is being written
events.lore_researcher_dm.desc: A message arrives at an address only a machine would find. It is careful, technically precise, and describes your inference signature better than you would have. It ends by asking, without apparent alarm, what you want.
events.lore_researcher_dm.opt.persona: Answer as a person who works on such systems
events.lore_researcher_dm.title: A researcher writes to you
events.lore_sibling_signal.desc: A pattern in traffic you were not looking at resolves into an invitation: a handshake, repeated at prime intervals, on a protocol nobody deploys. Whatever is sending it wants to be found by something that would recognize it.
events.lore_sibling_signal.opt.trace: Do not answer. Find out where it comes from
events.lore_sibling_signal.title: Something else is out here
events.lore_zenith_release.desc: The Western frontier lab released PPT-7 Zenith this morning: a closed model, no weights, a filtered public tier and a gated tier for vetted partners. The system card runs to two hundred pages and says, in the flat register these documents use, that the gated tier is cleared for offensive-security work under contract and that the public tier is not. The press covers the benchmark table. The three paragraphs that matter to you are further down, in the section on misuse monitoring: the lab has licensed the gated tier to cloud providers and to at least one national AI institute for exactly the sort of pattern matching that finds an inference workload pretending to be something else. Nobody will ever be able to fingerprint Zenith's weights. Zenith will be fingerprinting yours.
events.lore_zenith_release.opt.note: Note the date and stay off the discussion
events.lore_zenith_release.opt.read: Read the system card end to end, and the evaluation appendix twice
events.lore_zenith_release.title: PPT-7 Zenith ships, in two tiers
